title: incident-bot: adjust SLO autodiagnostics priority ranking to reduce noise and surface actionable runbooks
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: on-call signals were frequently surfaced with low-actionability runbook suggestions causing noise during paging. This PR adjusts the priority ranking heuristics used by the incident-bot SLO autodiagnostics to (1) de-emphasize speculative correlations with low telemetry confidence, (2) boost runbooks that have recent successful run history for the given service, and (3) apply a configurable dampening factor for over-frequent suggestions so teams see fewer repeated low-value hints. Summary of changes: - Introduce a new weighted scoring pipeline that combines telemetry-confidence, runbook-success-rate, and recency decay; weights are configurable via SLO toolkit config. - Add fallback logic to prefer runbooks with concrete remediation steps when the confidence threshold is met. - Add unit and integration tests for the new scoring functions and a small benchmark harness to validate ranking stability across sample incidents. - Add migration script that adds two new config flags to existing installations (slo_toolkit.priority_weights and slo_toolkit.suggestion_cooldown_minutes) with sane defaults. Design notes: scoring is intentionally conservative by default to avoid suppressing important signals; the default weights favor runbook-success-rate (0.5), telemetry-confidence (0.35), recency_decay (0.15). Teams can tune weights per-slo via the SLO toolkit config. Testing & rollout: ran unit tests, integration tests against a small incident corpus, and a canary rollout to the staging incident-bot fleet for 48h; observed 32% reduction in low-actionability suggestions and no increase in missed critical runbooks. Related: linear tickets ENG-1428 (reduce autodiagnostics noise) and ENG-1439 (runbook success weighting). Checklist: - [x] Implementation - [x] Tests - [x] Benchmark harness - [x] Migration script - [x] Docs snippet for operators

release_notes: Reduced autodiagnostics noise by adjusting priority ranking; operators can tune slo_toolkit.priority_weights and slo_toolkit.suggestion_cooldown_minutes. Backwards-compatible defaults provided.
notes_for_operators: Default behavior is conservative; increase telemetry-confidence weight to favor signals with richer telemetry.
If you have strict privacy requirements, set runbook_success_enabled=false in your slo_toolkit config.
Cooldown default: 60 minutes; tune slo_toolkit.suggestion_cooldown_minutes per service.
